source_identity_note: Receipts identify the base commit plus the actual uncommitted source fingerprint. This is not a future C6 freeze or release identity.
root_cause: After a synchronous standalone LocalCAS commit failure, ObjectService could persist an aborted intent but its generic discard deliberately skipped protected stages. Anonymous-only staging recovery could not reclaim those protected paths. Known storage-wrapped timeout/unknown errors were also incorrectly classified as aborted.
repair: Only the raw standalone store.commit failure branch passes its invocation-owned stage to finish_operation_intent. A matching successful aborted acknowledgement permits discarding that protected LocalCAS path. Known storage wrappers are unwrapped for uncertainty; unknown outcomes and unconfirmed aborts retain bytes. Post-commit hook, metadata publication, cluster and custom-store failures receive no new deletion authority.

failures_observed.test: confirmed abort reclaims four owned protected stages and preserves other bytes
reader commit failure reclaims its stage only after confirmed abort
nested storage uncertainty keeps protected stages and records unknown

verified_assertions: Four live concurrent writers share an operation ID but own distinct nonce paths. After injected synchronous commit :enospc failures, all wait at the abort acknowledgement barrier with baseline29 plus61440 temporary bytes. Confirmed aborts return temporary bytes to baseline29.
Another protected stage retains its29 bytes and a preexisting CAS object retains exact content.
Reader commit failure returns the original error and final reader state; confirmed abort leaves zero temporary bytes.
Storage-wrapped timeout, unknown and unknown_transaction_outcome record unknown and retain complete protected stages.
Abort backend timeout and compare failure retain complete protected stages.
Custom-store discard behavior and cluster aggregate-error retention remain unchanged.
Existing post-commit orphan and uncertain-publication tests continue passing.

fault_fixture: Real LocalCAS and isolated managed Context roots, with the existing per-call :sync durability fault hook and message barriers. Intent acknowledgements are controlled test adapters; no VM-wide config, sleep-based race, real ENOSPC, host disk fill or service interruption.

review.scope: Independent diff review reported by the coordinator; no separate automated review receipt is claimed.

limitations: Cleanup requires the current live caller to still own the exact staged path, a pre-metadata standalone LocalCAS commit failure, and a positive acknowledgement matching the operation ID and aborted state.
An aborted intent remains mutable; this change adds no directory sweep, terminal-state reinterpretation, grace change or deletion authority based on reading an aborted record.
Failed unlink is ignored by the existing error-return path and may leave bytes. LocalCAS.discard does not fsync the staging directory, so crash-durable absence is not established.
Process death before cleanup, uncertain commit outcomes and unconfirmed abort transitions can retain protected bytes.
Unit fixtures exercise acknowledgement gating using stubs. They do not prove durable-backend transition or crash/restart cleanup; unchanged fault and ENOSPC lanes remain required in full acceptance.
The original C5 CopyObject filesystem error remains unknown. This reproduces and repairs the proven retention mechanism without claiming to reproduce that original error.
This scoped23-test pass is not A30 resource, restart, C6 full acceptance, aggregate or release certification. Future candidate freezing and authoritative lanes remain coordinator-owned.
